correctness.rationale: Under the probability integral transform, the exact two-sided statistic is defined by a selected unweighted KS maximizing rank. A high ratio forces that rank near an endpoint. Only ranks 1 and n can contribute at order t^-2; other configurations require at least two observations in an O(t^-2) endpoint interval and have probability O_n(t^-4). The n! uniform-order-statistic density and n-1 disjoint exact intervals give the lower-corner integral; reflection doubles it. Stable quadratic root yields coefficient 2(n-1)!/n^n and the moment threshold via the tail-integral identity. The included independent checker passed 96 tests; the proof does not use its Monte Carlo as evidence for infinity.

originality.rationale: A full reading of the publicly available 2022 preprint identified only an exact one-sided CDF (Theorem 2.1) and a weak two-sided limit (Theorem 2.3), not the claimed fixed-n two-sided Pareto-tail coefficient. The two-sided argmax is chosen before weighting and therefore is not obtained by maximizing the separately weighted one-sided tests. Exact two-corner volume plus an O_n(t^-4) noncorner bound supplies a distinct scientific statement. Targeted published-literature and published-record searches found no theorem with this coefficient; historical-priority risk remains.

value.rationale: The fixed-n two-sided tail determines far-tail null quantiles and shows that variance-based calibration is mathematically invalid at every finite n even though an ordinary n->infinity weak limit exists. The factorial coefficient quantifies why this pathology becomes extremely rare at larger samples. This exact intrinsic extreme-null property of a published two-sided test is a natural motivated invariant, not an arbitrary slice.
